label: Cardiovascular Effects of Air Pollution and Noise in Stockholm
other synonyms: Cardiovascular Effects of Air pollution and Noise Study|Cardiovascular Effects of Air Pollution and Noise Study|Cardiovascular Effects of Air Pollution and Noise in Stockholm study|CEANS
example quote: Recruiting individuals from Stockholm County the Cardiovascular Effects of Air pollution and Noise Study (CEANS) cohort was included.
definition: A pooling of four population-based cohorts from Stockholm County, Sweden (the Stockholm Diabetes Prevention Programme, a random sample of 60-year-olds known as SIXTY, the Stockholm-resident participants of the Screening Across the Lifespan Twin study, and the Swedish National Study on Aging and Care in Kungsholmen), recruited between 1992 and 2004 and analysed together to study long-term exposure to ambient air pollution and noise as risk factors for cardiovascular disease.
location quote: Pooled data from the 4 cohorts from Stockholm, Sweden: SNAC-K, SALT/Twin gene, 60 y/IMPROVE, and SDPP.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CEANS (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CEANS), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue record is empty apart from the id (it comes from the EXPANSE network). CEANS is not a separately recruited cohort: every source describes it as four existing Stockholm cohorts pooled for air-pollution and noise studies (ESCAPE, ELAPSE, EXPANSE), so it is an aggregation. Its members (SDPP, SIXTY/60-year-olds, SALT, SNAC-K) are not in COHO; COHO's TwinGene Study (COHO:0000193) is a sub-study of SALT, and ESCAPE names the member 'SALT/Twin gene', but CEANS used all Stockholm-resident SALT twins, so TwinGene is not listed as a member. Label follows ESCAPE and EXPANSE ('...Noise in Stockholm'); the Swedish multicohort papers call it '...Noise Study', kept as synonyms (with the capitalisation variants). The design reference is Korek et al. 2015 (stroke in four Stockholm cohorts), not read.

Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry NBC1967-1976 (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/NBC1967-1976), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue record is empty: id and name are both 'NBC1967-1976', type 'Cohort study', no country, description or website; it belongs to the EPHOR network. No paper or web page uses the string 'NBC1967-1976'. The likely referent is the Norwegian register-based cohort of everyone born in Norway 1967-1976 used by the National Institute of Occupational Health (STAMI, an EPHOR partner; its other EPHOR entry NWAC is the Norwegian Working Age Cohort, Nor-Work), but no source links the catalogue id to that cohort, and the cohort has no name of its own beyond descriptions ('Norwegian birth cohort of 1967-1976'). The record above is the candidate if the curator accepts the identification; the example quote does not use a name because the papers never name it. Not in COHO under any name. Left unresolved rather than minted on an inference.

label: My Purchases cohort
other synonyms: Mine indkøb kohorten|Mine Indkøb|My Purchases|My purchases cohort
example quote: The My Purchases cohort has had ongoing recruitment since June 2021.
definition: A cohort of adult Danish residents who, since June 2021, have consented through a web application run by Statens Serum Institut to donate the digital receipts of their consumer purchases, linked through their personal identification number to national health registers, to study how purchases, diet and household lifestyle exposures affect health.
location quote: All Danish residents 18 years and older with a valid digital signature (MitID) and an account with the digital receipt solution can donate information about their purchases for research purposes.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CON (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CON), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A defined, consenting group of Danish adults whose purchase receipts are collected and linked to registers, run by Statens Serum Institut as part of the Human Exposome Assessment Platform (HEAP); a cohort, not in COHO (the suggested matches Project MinE, Aichi_Con and ESTAMPA are unrelated). The catalogue id and acronym is 'CON'; the cohort's own names are 'My Purchases cohort' (design paper) and 'Mine Indkøb' (website), with the catalogue's local name 'Mine indkøb kohorten'. The only paper found is the design paper, which analyses the cohort's data and serves as the example.

definition: A prospective cohort of persons aged 45 to 64 years in the Netherlands, stratified by age and employment status, followed from 2010 by the Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research TNO through online questionnaires on work characteristics, health, employment transitions, work ability and productivity, to study sustainable work participation of older workers; a second group was recruited in 2015.
location quote: STREAM is an ongoing prospective cohort among persons aged 45 to 64 years in the Netherlands stratified by age and employment status.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry STREAM (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/STREAM), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The capitalisation 'Study on TRansitions...' used in PMID:32414410 spells out the acronym and is kept as a synonym. label: Swedish Cervical Screening Cohort
other synonyms: Cervical Screening Cohort|Cervical screening cohort|Swedish cervical screening cohort
example quote: the TCGA dataset and the Swedish cervical screening cohort
definition: A cohort of women screened for human papillomavirus and cervical abnormalities in the capital region of Sweden, in the organised screening programme and in non-organised testing, enrolled from 2011 by the Center for Cervical Cancer Elimination at Karolinska Institutet and Karolinska University Hospital, with biobanked cervical samples and individual screening data updated from the Swedish National Cervical Screening Registry (NKCx), for long-term follow-up studies of cervical cancer and other diseases.
location quote: The CSC contains stored cervical cells from almost the entire screening population of women in the capital region of Stockholm, Sweden.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CSC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CSC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue's 'Cervical screening cohort' (CSC) is the HEAP cohort described in the 2024 data descriptor, which uses the same name and acronym. Its website is that of the national screening registry (NKCx) from which the cohort's data are updated, and its description ('all women resident in Sweden aged 23-70') and start year 1964 (the start of the Swedish screening programme) describe the registry and programme; the cohort itself enrols women screened in the Stockholm region from 2011. NKCx is not in COHO either; if the curator wants the national registry as its own term, it would be a separate cohort. Not in COHO; suggested matches are unrelated screening studies. Label from the data descriptor's title.

label: Dutch Famine Birth Cohort
other synonyms: Hongerwinter Onderzoek|Dutch famine birth cohort study|Dutch famine birth cohort|Dutch Famine Birth Cohort study
example quote: 801 plasma samples of members of the Dutch famine birth cohort were assessed for lipidomics and leptin at age 58.
definition: A historical birth cohort of singletons born alive and at term in the Wilhelmina Gasthuis in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, around the time of the 1944–1945 Dutch famine (1943–1947), traced and studied by Amsterdam UMC since 1994 through repeated interviews, examinations, biological samples, imaging and registry linkage, to investigate the effects of acute maternal undernutrition during specific stages of gestation on later health, particularly cardiovascular and metabolic disease, ageing and mental health.
location quote: Cohort profile: the Dutch famine birth cohort (DFBC)- a prospective birth cohort study in the Netherlands.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry DFBC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/DFBC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A defined historical birth cohort from one Amsterdam hospital, studied since 1994; not in COHO under any name. It is distinct from the Dutch Hunger Winter Families Study (Leiden), which is not in COHO either. Label as in the cohort profile's title (with its acronym DFBC); the catalogue's name 'Dutch Famine Birth Cohort study' and the website's Dutch name 'Hongerwinter Onderzoek' are synonyms, as are the lower-case variants the papers use.

label: Diabetes Prediction in Skåne
other synonyms: DiPiS study|Diabetes Prediction in Skåne study|DiPiS
example quote: influence the risk of developing type 1 diabetes (T1D) using data from the prospective Diabetes Prediction in Skåne (DiPiS) study.
definition: A prospective, population-based cohort of children born in Skåne, Sweden, between September 2000 and August 2004 who were screened as newborns for risk of type 1 diabetes, with children at increased risk followed with yearly capillary blood samples for islet autoantibodies from two to 15 years of age or until diabetes onset, to investigate the genetic and environmental factors contributing to or triggering type 1 diabetes.
location quote: The aim of this study was to analyse glycaemic control over a longer period, past the period of partial remission, after diagnosis in children followed before diagnosis in the Swedish Diabetes Prediction in Skåne (DiPiS) study compared with children of equal age not enrolled in pre-diabetes follow-up, receiving equivalent diabetes care.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry DiPiS (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/DiPiS), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue entry is the DiPiS biobank (BBMRI-ERIC SE_2328, via the HEDIMED network) with no name beyond the acronym; the biobank holds the samples of the Diabetes Prediction in Skåne study, a Swedish newborn-screening cohort for type 1 diabetes, so the term is for that cohort. Not in COHO (checked DiPiS, Skåne, TEDDY). The newborn screening covered all consenting births in Skåne (questionnaires at 2 months from over 23,000 children), with intensive follow-up of those at increased risk.

label: Finnish HPV vaccination cohort
other synonyms: HPV vaccination cohort|HPV-Rokotiitus|NCT00534638
example quote: from the Finnish HPV vaccination cohort
definition: The participants of a community-randomised phase IV trial in which early adolescents born 1992–1995 and resident in 33 Finnish communities were invited in 2007–2009 and assigned by community to gender-neutral HPV16/18 vaccination, HPV16/18 vaccination of girls with hepatitis B vaccination of boys, or gender-neutral hepatitis B vaccination, and followed up with cervicovaginal sampling from 18.5 years of age, to compare the overall and herd effects of gender-neutral and girls-only HPV vaccination.
location quote: Human papillomavirus seroprevalence in pregnant women following gender-neutral and girls-only vaccination programs in Finland: A cross-sectional cohort analysis following a cluster randomized trial.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry HPV (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/HPV), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue entry is the Finnish community-randomised HPV vaccination trial of 2007-2009 (its description, start year and website), a defined group of trial participants, so a cohort; not in COHO. The trial has no proper name: the catalogue calls it 'HPV vaccination cohort', its website 'HPV-Rokotiitus', and the HEAP paper HPV-KITE 'the Finnish HPV vaccination cohort', used here as the label; the curator may prefer another. The catalogue acronym 'HPV' is kept as an acronym as the rules require although it is the virus's abbreviation. Several of the catalogue's publications (the 2006 enrolment papers and the ten-year follow-up, PMID:28821519) are about different, earlier Finnish cohorts (PATRICIA and HPV-012 trial participants and an unvaccinated cohort enrolled 2003-2005) and are not part of this term. The example quote from HPV-KITE names the cohort without describing it; its identity rests on the paper's citation of the community-vaccination study. Could not read: PMID:25593103 full text (closed; abstract read).

other synonyms: TirolGESUND Lifestyle Atlas|Tyrol Lifestyle Atlas|Multiomic Lifestyle Intervention study|TirolGESUND: General Exercise, Smoking Undone, and Nutrition Diet|General Exercise, Smoking Undone, and Nutrition Diet|General Exercise, Smoking undone, and nutrition diet|TirolGESUND
example quote: The TirolGESUND study enrolled 156 women aged 30 to 60 years into one of two parallel six-month interventions based on lifestyle risk factors: intermittent fasting (n=114, BMI ≥25) or smoking cessation (n=42, ≥10 cigarettes/day for ≥5 years)
definition: A lifestyle intervention study of healthy women aged 30 to 60 in Tyrol, Austria, run by the EUTOPS Institute of the University of Innsbruck from 2021, in which women with a raised BMI followed six months of intermittent fasting (randomised to a ketogenic supplement or not) and heavy smokers underwent smoking cessation, with repeated sampling of several tissues to study how DNA methylation and other multi-omic biomarkers of health, ageing and cancer risk respond to lifestyle change.
location quote: EUTOPS Institute at the University of Innsbruck, Austria
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry LSC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/LSC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. TirolGESUND (official title 'TirolGESUND: General Exercise, Smoking Undone, and Nutrition Diet', NCT05678426, ISRCTN15374182; the catalogue's external id 20210420-2560 is the Innsbruck hospital study-register number) is a 2021-2022 single-site intervention study of 156 Tyrolean women (intermittent fasting arm, smoking cessation arm) at the EUTOPS Institute, Hall in Tirol / University of Innsbruck; the 'Lifestyle Atlas' is its multi-omic data portal, so the catalogue's name is the resource, not the study. A trial's participants are a cohort. Not in COHO. The example is a bioRxiv preprint with no PMID (no journal version found in Europe PMC). The country quote only places the coordinating institute in Austria; the ClinicalTrials.gov record (structured field, not quotable prose) gives the site as Hall in Tirol, Austria, and the title says 'Healthy Female Tyrolean Volunteers'. ACRONYM CLASH: the catalogue id LSC is also the acronym of the Lovelace Smokers Cohort (COHO:0002019); both terms need the editor note. Label choice ('TirolGESUND study', as the preprint calls it) is for the curator; the formal title is given as a synonym. Not minted on 2026-09-25: no paper with a PMID that used the cohort (its example is a preprint); the record above is kept for when one appears.

example quote: In Cyprus, participant recruitment took place between October 2023 and January 2024 and data collection for the baseline assessment was conducted from January 2024 to June 2024.
definition: The Cypriot site of the CHILDREN_FIRST multi-country prospective exposome cohort: children in the first grade of randomly selected public primary schools in Cyprus, recruited from October 2023 by the Cyprus University of Technology with the biobank of the University of Cyprus and assessed every year until the end of primary school with questionnaires, urine and saliva samples and home and school environmental measurements, to study how the exposome shapes early risk of cardiometabolic, neurodevelopmental and respiratory disease.
location quote: In Cyprus, participant recruitment took place between October 2023 and January 2024 and data collection for the baseline assessment was conducted from January 2024 to June 2024.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CHILDREN FIRST (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CHILDREN%20FIRST), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue entry (Cyprus, 2023-2029, pointing to childrenfirstcy.com) is the Cypriot Children's Health and Environment Observatory, which calls itself 'CHILDREN_FIRST – The Cypriot Children's Health and Environment Observatory' and says it is part of the Mediterranean CHILDREN_FIRST network. The protocol describes CHILDREN_FIRST as one multi-country cohort with sites in Cyprus, Greece and Albania, of which only Cyprus had recruited (Greece had done feasibility work); if the curator prefers one term for the whole multi-country cohort, label it CHILDREN_FIRST and make this a sub-cohort, or widen this definition. The only paper is the protocol, which reports the Cypriot recruitment, so it serves as the example; no results paper was found in Europe PMC. The Greek name comes from the site's about page.

input name: Observation of Cardiovascular Risks and Health in Luxembourg
label: Observation of Cardiovascular Risks and Health in Luxembourg
other synonyms: Observation des Risques et de la Santé Cardio-Vasculaire au Luxembourg|Observation of Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Luxembourg|Observation of cardiovascular risk factors in Luxembourg
example quote: Data were from the ORISCAV-LUX 2 study, a national cross-sectional survey of cardiovascular risk factors in the Luxembourgish adult population
definition: A nationwide population-based study of adults living in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, run by the Luxembourg Institute of Health, whose first wave (2007-2009) examined a random sample of residents and whose second wave (2016-2018) re-examined them together with new participants from the civil registry, another national health examination survey and volunteers, with questionnaires, clinical measurements and blood, urine and hair samples, to describe the prevalence and evolution of cardiovascular risk factors.
location quote: ORISCAV-LUX (Observation des Risques et de la Santé Cardio-Vasculaire au Luxembourg = Observation of Cardiovascular Risks and Health in Luxembourg) was the first nationwide epidemiological study aimed at establishing an objective picture of the prevalence of lifestyle-related risk factors for cardiovascular disease in the general population residing in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ORISCAV-LUX-II (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ORISCAV-LUX-II), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue entry is the second wave (ORISCAV-LUX 2, 2016-2018) of LIH's ORISCAV-LUX study; its name is the whole study's. The second wave followed up the first wave's participants (660 of them) and added new random samples and volunteers (PMID:30717671: 'In 2016, the second wave ORISCAV-LUX study was initiated to follow-up the same baseline sample of participants.'), and later papers treat both waves as one cohort, so one term for the study is proposed, carrying the wave-2 names as acronyms. If the curator wants the second wave as its own term, it would be a sub-cohort of this one. Luxembourg is not in gaz_xrefs.tsv (DBpedia resource Luxembourg); the country also follows from the name. None of the suggested COHO terms is related.

label: Barcelona Life Study Cohort
other synonyms: BiSC Project
example quote: Data came from 389 pregnant women in the Barcelona Life Study Cohort (BiSC).
definition: An exposome birth cohort of pregnant women enrolled between October 2018 and April 2021 at three tertiary university hospitals in Barcelona, Spain (Hospital Sant Joan de Déu, Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau and Hospital Clínic de Barcelona) and their primary healthcare centres, and of their children, followed from the first trimester of pregnancy through delivery into childhood to study the socio-environmental and genetic determinants of foetal and child health, growth and development and of maternal mental and physical health during and after pregnancy.
location quote: The enrolment of the BiSC participants (n=1080) was carried out between October 2018 and April 2021 at three tertiary university hospitals in Barcelona, Spain, including Hospital Sant Joan de Déu, Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau, and Hospital Clínic de Barcelona, and their corresponding primary healthcare centres.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry BiSC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/BiSC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. BiSC is an ISGlobal-led exposome birth cohort in Barcelona (ERC-funded), with mothers recruited in pregnancy 2018-2021 and children followed postnatally. No COHO term covers it: the suggested matches (Barcelona-1, Triple A Barcelona Study, LIFE studies) are unrelated. 'BiSC Project' is the name the website uses for its project page. The design paper is the IJE cohort profile PMID:38725298, which could replace the website as definition source once its text is available. Could not read: PMID:38725298 full text (cohort profile, requested; not needed for the record).

Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry EXOMAIR (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/EXOMAIR), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. EXOMAIR is a research project, not a group of people. It runs 2024-2026 under ISCIII grant PI23/01032, is coordinated at ISGlobal, and its full title is 'Hacia una Medicina de Precisión: Análisis del Exposoma y Omicas usando Inteligencia Artificial Explicable para estudiar su impacto durante la vida en la Obesidad, Insulino Resistencia y salud metabólica'. The ISGlobal page says it analyses two existing cohorts: 'Se llevarán a cabo enfoques multiómicos y de exposoma a partir de dos cohortes ya existentes: PUBMEP (N=198) e IBEROMICs (N=753).' (https://www.isglobal.org/-/exomair). Both of those cohorts are separate entries of this catalogue (PUBMEP in this batch, IBEROMICS elsewhere). The catalogue's 'hospital cohort' wording describes the data the project uses. It is not a consortium of cohorts either, only one funded project, so it is not an aggregation. Nothing to mint.

input name: Puberty and metabolic risk in obese children. Epigenetic alterations and pathophysiological and diagnostic implications
label: Puberty and metabolic risk in obese children. Epigenetic alterations and pathophysiological and diagnostic implications
other synonyms: PUBMEP study
example quote: Hence, the PUBMEP study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of MetS and the progression of cardiometabolic risk factors related to it from prepuberty to puberty in a cohort of Spanish children.
definition: A multicentre longitudinal follow-up in Spain (Santiago de Compostela, Córdoba, Zaragoza and Granada) of children who had taken part in the GENOBOX study before puberty and were re-examined after reaching puberty, grouped by obesity and insulin resistance status, to study the progression of metabolic syndrome and cardiometabolic risk factors from prepuberty to puberty and to find biomarkers and epigenetic marks of metabolic complications during puberty.
location quote: Hence, the PUBMEP study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of MetS and the progression of cardiometabolic risk factors related to it from prepuberty to puberty in a cohort of Spanish children.
parent quote: The PUBMEP is a longitudinal study based on the follow-up of a cohort of children who had previously participated in the GENOBOX study (22–29).
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry PUBMEP (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/PUBMEP), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. PUBMEP is a Spanish multicentre follow-up at puberty of children first studied, before puberty, in GENOBOX. GENOBOX is a separate entry of this catalogue (in another batch), not yet in COHO, so the parent is given as the catalogue id GENOBOX and depends on GENOBOX being minted; drop the parent if it is not. The label is the project title as the University of Granada (UCEENS) gives it, and the catalogue uses the same title. No source expands the acronym, and papers call it 'the PUBMEP study', so the curator may prefer 'PUBMEP study' as the label. The catalogue's 96 children are the epigenetic subsample. The 2022 paper describes 191 who agreed to take part, and ISGlobal gives N=198. No COHO term matches: the suggested Leipzig and other childhood obesity cohorts are different studies. The EXOMAIR project in this batch analyses PUBMEP.

Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry TEEC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/TEEC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue describes a real cohort, about 400 older adults in southern Taiwan recruited 2022-2025 with biosamples, but no website, publication or host institution for it could be found, so there is no example study and no source beyond the catalogue. The catalogue says it is 'nested', but not in which parent cohort. One guess is the Taiwan Initiative for Geriatric Epidemiological Research (TIGER, southern Taiwan, collects environmental exposures and metabolomics), but nothing links them, so no parent is given. It is not the same people as any COHO term: Taiwan Biobank, the NCI Taiwan cohort and the Taiwan diabetes studies are unrelated. The draft fields above come from the catalogue alone and could be used to mint it once a publication appears (or as a placeholder, if the curator wants one). Could not read: any publication or website of TEEC, PMID:40737520 full text, to see whether it used TEEC.

input name: Study of Secondary Exposures to Pesticides Across Childhood, Adolescence and Adulthood
label: Study of Secondary Exposure to Pesticides among Children, Adolescents, and Adults
other synonyms: Study of Secondary Exposures to Pesticides Across Childhood, Adolescence and Adulthood|Study of secondary exposure to pesticides among children, adolescents, and adults|Secondary Exposure to Pesticides Among Children, Adolescents, and Adults (ESPINA) study|ESPINA study|ESPINA Study
example quote: This article presents urinary pesticide metabolite concentrations for 665 participants in the “Study of Secondary Exposure to Pesticides among Children, Adolescents, and Adults” (ESPINA)
definition: A prospective cohort set up in 2008 of children living in the agricultural (floricultural) community of Pedro Moncayo County, Pichincha, Ecuador, recruited to include a balanced mix of children who did and did not live with a floricultural or agricultural worker and followed with repeated examinations into adolescence and adulthood, run by the University of California San Diego with Fundación Cimas del Ecuador to study the health effects of pesticide and other agrochemical exposures from childhood to adulthood.
location quote: ESPINA is a prospective cohort established in 2008 that aims to investigate the impacts of pesticide exposure on development from childhood to adulthood in individuals living within the agricultural community of Pedro Moncayo, Pichincha, Ecuador.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ESPINA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ESPINA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. ESPINA is UCSD's pesticide cohort in Pedro Moncayo, Ecuador: children examined in 2008, with follow-ups in 2016 and 2022 and later ones, and extra participants recruited at the follow-ups. No COHO term covers it: the suggested matches are unrelated. The label is the expansion the 2025 data paper puts in quotation marks. The catalogue's name ('...Across Childhood, Adolescence and Adulthood') and the paper's own variants are given as synonyms. The website mentions an ancillary study, ESPINA-EMCT, that is part of the same cohort. It is not a separate entry.

label: Rome Longitudinal Study
other synonyms: Rome longitudinal study
example quote: We used the Rome Longitudinal Study, the administrative cohort of residents in Rome who filled in the 2001 population census.
definition: An administrative cohort of the residents of Rome, Italy, enrolled from population census returns (the 2001 census and the census of 9 October 2011) linked to the municipal population registry, and followed by record linkage with administrative health databases, with baseline residential addresses linked to environmental exposures such as air pollution, temperature and greenness. It is run by the Department of Epidemiology of the Lazio Regional Health Service (ASL Roma 1) to study social, occupational and environmental determinants of health.
location quote: We enrolled 1,739,277 individuals 30 + years from the 2011 census in Rome, Italy, and followed them up until 2019.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ROLS (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ROLS), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The Rome Longitudinal Study is a census-based administrative cohort of the whole resident population of Rome, run by the Lazio Department of Epidemiology. It is a defined population followed by record linkage, so it is a cohort. The catalogue describes the enrolment at the 2011 census, followed to 2019. Earlier papers use an enrolment at the 2001 census, with the same study name. The term is defined to cover both, since no source presents them as separately named cohorts. 'RoLS' is the form papers use (e.g. PMID:39032743, 'the Italian Rome Longitudinal Study (RoLS)'), and 'ROLS' is the catalogue's id. No COHO term matches: the suggested longitudinal studies are unrelated.

input name: Prevention Cube: data warehouse for detection and evaluation of trends of occupational diseases (Precube)
label: Prevention Cube
other synonyms: Prevention Cube: data warehouse for detection and evaluation of trends of occupational diseases (Precube)|Prevention Cube: data warehouse for detection and evaluation of trends of occupational diseases
example quote: We investigated work and health's associations in a specific sector: the agricultural sector and for a specific and frequent health complaint: sore throat; using PRECUBE dataset of the Belgian Occupational Health and Safety, containing 381.615 occupational health observations.
definition: An occupational cohort of the employees of employers in Belgium that chose IDEWE as their External Service for Prevention and Protection at Work, followed from 1993 through the records of their legally required occupational health surveillance. IDEWE pools the records in a data warehouse for research on work-related diseases and sector-specific health problems.
location quote: We investigated work and health's associations in a specific sector: the agricultural sector and for a specific and frequent health complaint: sore throat; using PRECUBE dataset of the Belgian Occupational Health and Safety, containing 381.615 occupational health observations.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry Precube (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/Precube), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A borderline call. The catalogue and the 2015 paper call Precube a 'data warehouse' of IDEWE's occupational health surveillance records. CHECKM lists data warehouses as not cohorts, but this one covers a defined group of people: all employees of employers affiliated to IDEWE, a Belgian external prevention service, followed with repeated examinations since 1993. The OMega-X cohort profile (PMID:42615545) treats it as one of its 24 occupational cohorts ('Some, however, followed workers from the 1950s (SLFF), 1960s (Danish Styrene cohort, Nor-Work), 1970s (DOC*X, SNOW, SWIP), 1980s (HUNT), or 1990s (ECRHS, GAZEL, PRECUBE, RHINE, the SUS Study) for decades.'). It is therefore given as a cohort. If the curator reads the CHECKM rule strictly it becomes 'not a cohort'. The label 'Prevention Cube' is the expansion only the catalogue gives; papers write PRECUBE. OMega-X (the European Occupational Exposome Mega Cohort Consortium) is not in COHO, so no parent is given, but it would be the aggregation to add Precube to. Could not read: PMID:26503980 full text (closed; not needed for the verdict).

input name: Health, Alcohol and Psychosocial factors In Eastern Europe
label: Czech Health, Alcohol and Psychosocial factors In Eastern Europe study
other synonyms: Czech HAPIEE study|Czech HAPIEE cohort|Health, Alcohol and Psychosocial factors In Eastern Europe
example quote: Lack of an association between left-handedness and APOE polymorphism in a large sample of adults: results of the Czech HAPIEE study.
definition: The Czech Republic cohort of the HAPIEE study: a random sample of men and women aged 45-69 years, stratified by sex and age and selected from population registers in six Czech towns (Havířov/Karviná, Hradec Králové, Jihlava, Kroměříž, Liberec and Ústí nad Labem), examined at baseline in 2002-2005 and followed through re-examinations (most recently in 2023-2024) and linkage to national health registers, with geocoded addresses linked to exposome and census data. The aim is to study psychosocial, behavioural and environmental risk factors for cardiovascular and other chronic diseases and for ageing outcomes.
location quote: The HAPIEE (Health, Alcohol and Psychosocial factors In Eastern Europe) study consists of three cohorts in Novosibirsk (Russia), Krakow (Poland) and six centres in the Czech Republic (Havirov/Karvina, Hradec Kralove, Jihlava, Kromeriz, Liberec and Usti nad Labem).
parent quote: The HAPIEE (Health, Alcohol and Psychosocial factors In Eastern Europe) study consists of three cohorts in Novosibirsk (Russia), Krakow (Poland) and six centres in the Czech Republic (Havirov/Karvina, Hradec Kralove, Jihlava, Kromeriz, Liberec and Usti nad Labem).
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry HAPIEE-CZ (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/HAPIEE-CZ), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. This is the Czech arm of HAPIEE, which COHO already has as COHO:0000265, a single term for all four national cohorts. It is a separately recruited country cohort with its own cohort profile, so it is a new cohort with isSubCohortOf COHO:0000265, as CHECKM anticipates. The catalogue's description is that of the whole HAPIEE study, but its id, country (Czechia) and exposome geocoding point to the Czech cohort. The label is the Czech cohort's own name from the title of its 2026 cohort-profile preprint. The catalogue's name for this entry is the parent's full name, so it is not repeated as a synonym. The parent term's current example is the Siberian (Novosibirsk) branch on EGA, so it is untouched.

label: International Lipid-Based Nutrient Supplements Project-DYAD-Malawi
other synonyms: iLiNS-DYAD-Malawi|International Lipid‑Based Nutrient Supplements Project
example quote: children from rural Africa (participants from the iLINS-DYAD-M study conducted in Malawi)
definition: The participants of a randomised, single-blind controlled trial in rural Malawi (Mangochi, University of Malawi College of Medicine with Tampere University), part of the International Lipid-Based Nutrient Supplements (iLiNS) Project: pregnant women enrolled from 2011, and later their infants. The women received small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements, multiple micronutrients or iron-folic acid during pregnancy and lactation, and the infants were followed to test effects on birth size, child growth and development, with a later follow-up of the children at 9 years.
location quote: A Research Plan for a Randomised, Single-blind, Parallel Group Controlled Trial in Rural Malawi, Testing the Health Effects of Supplementing Maternal Diet During Pregnancy and Lactation and Infant Diet From 6 to 18 Months of Age With High-energy, Micronutrient Fortified Lipid-based Nutrient Supplements (LNS)
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry iLiNS DOSE iLiNS DYAD (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/iLiNS%20DOSE%20iLiNS%20DYAD), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue's name is that of the umbrella iLiNS Project, a research programme of several trials: DOSE and DYAD-M in Malawi, DYAD-G in Ghana, ZINC in Burkina Faso. Its acronym joins two Malawi trials, iLiNS-DOSE (infants enrolled at 6 months, 2009-2011) and iLiNS-DYAD-M. But its description, dates (2011-2015) and single country describe only iLiNS-DYAD-M, the mother-infant trial. The entry is therefore given as that trial's participants, the group of people it describes, under the full name given in PMID:30426668. The catalogue's umbrella name is kept as a synonym, because the catalogue tags this entry with it, but the curator may drop it if an iLiNS aggregation is ever minted. iLiNS-DOSE is a different set of participants and would be a separate term if wanted; the catalogue does not describe it. Malawi is not in gaz_xrefs.tsv: DBpedia resource Malawi. No COHO term matches (grep for iLiNS, DYAD, lipid-based: nothing). Could not read: PMID:25646337 full text (closed; abstract suffices).

label: New Hampshire Birth Cohort Study
other synonyms: New Hampshire birth cohort study|NH Birth Cohort Study
example quote: We investigated the association between As exposure and risk of glucose intolerance and GDM among 1151 women enrolled in the New Hampshire Birth Cohort Study.
definition: A prospective longitudinal cohort of pregnant women enrolled since 2009 at prenatal clinics in the Concord and Lebanon regions of New Hampshire, USA, by the Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth, and of their children, followed from early pregnancy into childhood to study how environmental contaminants, such as arsenic from private well water, affect the health of pregnant women and their children.
location quote: Beginning in 2009, with the help of medical providers in New Hampshire, the study staff at the Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth, began enrolling pregnant women at clinics in the Concord and Lebanon regions of New Hampshire.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry NHBCS (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/NHBCS), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. NHBCS is Dartmouth's pregnancy and birth cohort in New Hampshire, begun in 2009 and focused on arsenic and other contaminants in private well water. It has no COHO term: the suggested birth cohorts are unrelated. Its website says it takes part in the NIH Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Program ('Our data team and investigators interface with the Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Program to ensure that the scientific aspects of our study are sound.', https://www.protectkidshealth.com/about). ECHO is not in COHO, so no parent is given. The lower-case title form 'New Hampshire birth cohort study' is kept as a synonym under the capitalisation rule. The site says participants now come from New Hampshire and Vermont, but only the United States is asserted.

label: Shanghai Dapuqiao Aging and Cognition Study

input name: Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe
label: Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe
example quote: A Frailty Instrument for primary care: findings from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE)
definition: A multidisciplinary, cross-nationally harmonised longitudinal panel survey of people aged 50 and older, begun in 2004 in eleven European countries and Israel and extended to all EU member states and Switzerland, run as a European Research Infrastructure Consortium (SHARE-ERIC, coordinated from Munich and later Berlin), that collects data on health, biomarkers, cognition, employment, socio-economic status and social and family networks to study the effects of health, social, economic and environmental policies over the life course.
location quote: They constitute a balanced representation of the various regions in Europe, ranging from Scandinavia (Denmark and Sweden) through Central Europe (Austria, France, Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, and the Netherlands) to the Mediterranean (Spain, Italy and Greece). || Israel joined the SHARE framework in late 2004, being the first country in the Middle East to initiate a systematic study of its aging population. || Two 'new' EU member states - the Czech Republic and Poland - as well as Ireland joined SHARE in 2006 and participated in the second wave of data collection in 2006-07. || In 2010, Estonia, Hungary, Portugal and Slovenia joined SHARE Wave 4, which is the third regular panel wave of the survey following the SHARELIFE life history questionnaire. || The following countries collected data and are part of the scientific release: Austria, Belgium, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Germany, Denmark, Estonia, Spain, France, Israel, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Sweden, and Slovenia. || Additionally, Croatia participated in SHARE Wave 6 for the first time. || In 2017, the main data collection of Wave 7 took place in 28 countries - full coverage of the EU was achieved by including 8 new countries in SHARE: Finland, Lithuania, Latvia, Slovakia, Romania, Bulgaria, Malta and Cyprus.
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry SHARE (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/SHARE), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The pan-European panel survey of people 50+ (SHARE, 2004 onwards, 28 countries including Israel). Not in COHO: the COHO terms matching the name are other things (COHO:0000725 SHARE = Sinai-Helmsley Alliance for Research Excellence, an IBD cohort; COHO:0000604 SHARe = WHI SNP Health Association Resource; COHO:0001011 Genetics of SHARE = Scottish Health Research Register). The acronym SHARE is shared with COHO:0000725, so both terms need the editor note ("The acronym SHARE also denotes ..."); SHARe on COHO:0000604 differs only in case, so a case-insensitive overlap check may also want notes there. Luxembourg, Malta and Slovenia are not in gaz_xrefs.tsv (DBpedia names Luxembourg, Malta, Slovenia given). Country quotes come from SHARE's wave overview pages; Ireland took part in wave 2 only as far as those pages say. The HCAP sister study SHARE-HCAP is not part of this entry.

input name: Diagnostic Assessment of Dementia for the Longitudinal Aging Study in India
label: Harmonized Diagnostic Assessment of Dementia for the Longitudinal Aging Study in India

note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry LASI-DAD (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/LASI-DAD), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. definition: A population-based prospective mother-child cohort of pregnant women living in the Butajira Health and Demographic Surveillance Site, Meskan and Mareko district, Ethiopia, enrolled from 2017-2018 by the School of Public Health of Addis Ababa University and followed through pregnancy and after birth to study how maternal nutrition, mycotoxin exposure and mental health affect prenatal and postnatal growth and development.

No COHO term matches. The catalogue entry is the participants of trial NCT02807818 (80 pregnant adolescents and their children): Primeiros Laços is the Portuguese name of the intervention, which the papers also call the Young Caregiving (or Caring) Mothers Program, YCMP, and now the First Ties Program. A trial's participants are a cohort. The label is the catalogue's acronym and the name the trial papers use; the curator may prefer a label naming the trial (e.g. the ClinicalTrials.gov brief title 'A Home Visiting Program for Pregnant Youth to Promote Early Brain Development'). The trial id NCT02807818 could go in as a cross-reference. The catalogue's type is 'Clinical trial'. The participants live in the same western region of São Paulo as the ROC birth cohort (entry ROC of this check) but were separately recruited through primary care units; no source makes it a subcohort of ROC.

Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CAC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CAC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Cuenta de Alto Costo (the High-Cost Diseases Office of the Fondo Colombiano de Enfermedades de Alto Costo) is a Colombian health-system body to which insurers and providers must by law report every patient with certain high-cost diseases; it compiles and audits national administrative registries (the National Administrative Cancer Registry, and registries for HIV/AIDS, chronic kidney disease, haemophilia and other coagulopathies, rheumatoid arthritis and more), as the catalogue's own description lists. The entry is the agency and its bundle of mandatory disease registries, not a defined group of people recruited for study, so not a cohort (a health agency / data warehouse). A single registry drawn from it could be a cohort only if a study defines one; papers do analyse 'nationwide administrative registry cohorts' from CAC data (e.g. PMID:40171140, PMID:36742410, from Europe PMC titles), but these are analysis-specific samples, not the catalogue's entry. No COHO term matches; COHO:0001606's synonym 'Colombian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer' is unrelated.
